selected_clusters.name: ML Code and Asset Organization

values.description: Organizing ML implementation as maintainable object-oriented programs rather than primarily interactive cells.

values.label: Deployable and understandable model code
values.description: Generated modeling code is kept understandable, maintainable, and ready for production deployment.

values.label: Knowledge continuity after contributor departure

selected_clusters.name: ML Dependency and Service Structure
selected_clusters.description: How ML dependencies and cross-cutting services are specified, injected, and reproduced across environments.

values.description: Production packages, images, and runtime resources are declared so execution environments can be provisioned and reproduced. Development or notebook environments are not necessarily governed by the same dependency policy.

includes.description: Declares packages, images, and runtime resources required for production execution.

values.label: Explicit production dependencies with unpinned development environments

includes.description: Allowing notebook or model environments to rely on library versions that are not explicitly pinned across machines.

values.label: Centralized dependency-injected cross-cutting services
values.description: Shared functionality spanning ML layers or pipelines is organized centrally and supplied to components through dependency injection rather than being independently implemented or configured in each component.

includes.description: Organizes shared cross-layer functionality centrally and supplies it through dependency injection.

values.label: Dependency reproducibility concern

selected_clusters.name: ML Technology Selection Governance
selected_clusters.description: How teams select, constrain, and evaluate technologies and development toolkits for ML work.

selected_clusters.name: Data Ingestion Mechanism
selected_clusters.description: How source events and records are delivered into ML data workflows.

relations.reading: Choices on Data Ingestion Mechanism affect the outcomes of Training Execution and Scaling Strategy
relations.rationale: Ingestion mode, feature transformations, and available datasets determine training inputs, freshness, and execution requirements.

relations.reading: Choices on Data Ingestion Mechanism affect the outcomes of Production Monitoring and Adaptation
relations.rationale: Feature-generation frequency and incoming-data changes affect model behavior and retraining needs.

values.label: ETL-based feature ingestion
values.description: Batch extraction, transformation, and loading of row-level features from external data sources.

values.label: Streaming feature ingestion
values.description: Continuous or event-driven ingestion of base features from external sources.

values.label: Dual-path event and data ingestion
values.description: Routing interaction inputs simultaneously through low-latency event processing and durable dense-data processing.

values.label: Messaging-based data ingestion

values.label: Change-data-capture ingestion

criteria.name: Orthogonality
criteria.description: Every dimension is a distinct decision point: no two dimensions ask the same question, and no dimension's candidate decisions are really options of another dimension.
criteria.reason: Most dimensions represent distinct decisions, such as model serving interface (29), serving mode (31), runtime resources (26), and model evaluation (13). However, several dimensions overlap. Data ingestion (21) and dataset access/availability (24) both cover extraction, sourcing, APIs, and delivery; move values such as 24.1 API-mediated dataset access and 24.3 external curated dataset sourcing into 21, or narrow 24 to availability constraints. Data governance/preservation (42) overlaps lifecycle versioning and lineage in 20; move 20.4 data-to-model lineage management and the dataset-governance portions of 20.3/20.6 to 42. Training execution (3) contains distributed event computation (3.3), which answers ingestion/processing rather than training and should move to 21. Feature/data serving storage (43) also overlaps dataset access in 24 through storage and serving mechanisms; move 24.2 local consolidation to 43 or narrow 24 to access and availability requirements. These overlaps prevent the taxonomy from consistently maintaining one clearly distinct question per dimension.

criteria.name: Clarity
criteria.description: Dimension names and descriptions make the decision question clear, and value labels and descriptions make the alternatives distinguishable, so a reader could tell which dimension and value a passage about a design decision belongs to.
criteria.reason: Many dimensions have readable questions and distinctive values, such as 23 Data Labeling Strategy and 29 Model Serving Interface. However, several areas are unclear or overlapping: in 20 ML Artifact and Lifecycle Versioning, 20.3 Comprehensive ML lifecycle traceability, 20.5 Pipeline-based CI/CD governance, and 20.6 End-to-end reproducible lifecycle governance substantially duplicate one another; merge the overlapping values and retain one consolidated description. In 21 Data Ingestion Mechanism, transport choices such as 21.2 Streaming feature ingestion and 21.4 Messaging-based data ingestion overlap with source choices such as 21.7 Event-stream data sourcing and 21.8 Raw-dump data sourcing; reorganize these into separate existing decision questions. In 34 ML Workflow Execution Mode, 34.1, 34.2, and 34.3 address separation, offline execution, and instrumentation rather than clearly comparable alternatives; split or relocate them so each value set answers one clearly stated question. In 44 ML Interactive Development Environment, 44.2 Jupyter-and-IDE development workflow and 44.3 Cloud-hosted integrated notebook-and-IDE workflow are difficult to distinguish because the latter largely repeats the former with a hosting qualifier; merge them or make the hosting distinction explicit. In 46 ML Code and Asset Organization, code structure, collaboration, documentation, technology complexity, and several outcomes are combined; split the existing values into clearer code-organization and asset-governance questions.

criteria.name: Completeness
criteria.description: The taxonomy contains the major decision points implied by the use case, each with its main candidate decisions.
criteria.reason: The taxonomy represents the major workflow areas in the use case with decision points that have multiple candidate options: ingestion (21, nine accepted mechanisms), transformation and features (41), labeling (23, two alternatives), training and scaling (3), model selection and learning (27, 28), evaluation and testing (13, 14), packaging and serving (30, 31), monitoring and adaptation (6), and orchestration, release, infrastructure, and ownership (32, 33, 19, 39). Even narrower areas such as interactive development (44) and notebook execution (45) have several candidates, while outcomes are explicitly distinguished from decisions. No major workflow area lacks a multi-candidate decision point under the stated criterion.

criteria.name: Use case alignment
criteria.description: Every dimension serves the stated use case; none is out of its scope.
criteria.reason: Most dimensions are directly within the requested ML-system workflow, covering ingestion (21), transformation (41), training (3, 27, 28), evaluation (13), release (19), serving (29–31), and operations (6). The main scope issues are dimension 40, "ML Organizational and Process Approach," which focuses on culture, team structure, consultants, and delivery processes rather than architectural decisions; drop it or move only its infrastructure-relevant content into existing technical dimensions. Dimension 18, "ML Delivery and Problem Framing," is primarily product scoping and validation rather than system architecture; drop it or merge its production-constraint outcomes into an existing deployment or evaluation dimension. Dimension 37, "ML Technology Selection Governance," and dimension 44, "ML Interactive Development Environment," are tangential governance and tooling concerns; drop them or fold their technically relevant choices into dimensions 30 or 46.

criteria.name: No catch-alls
criteria.description: No dimension or value is a vague catch-all ('Other', 'Miscellaneous', 'General', 'Other approaches').
criteria.reason: The taxonomy generally avoids explicit 'Other' or 'Miscellaneous' buckets, but three catch-all areas remain. Dimension 38, "MLOps Automation and Composition," especially value 38.1 "Automated ML lifecycle workflows," bundles broad lifecycle automation without a defined decision boundary; split it into separate existing-content dimensions for lifecycle activity automation and toolchain composition, using values 38.1 versus 38.2–38.3 (and the related rejected values). Dimension 40, "ML Organizational and Process Approach," combines teams, roles, culture, process models, and iteration; split it into team/role structure (40.2, 40.3, 40.7, 40.8) and delivery/process model (40.1, 40.4–40.6). Dimension 46, "ML Code and Asset Organization," combines code structure, reusable assets, documentation, and production organization; split it into code/production organization and asset reuse/documentation using its existing values. These broad buckets are particularly problematic in a taxonomy intended to expose distinct workflow decisions from ingestion through operations.

criteria.name: Axis vs. value
criteria.description: Each dimension is a decision point with alternatives, not a single option presented as a dimension; each value is an option, not a sub-topic.
criteria.reason: The taxonomy contains many dimensions that combine multiple independent decisions or contain values that are decisions of their own. (1) Dimension 34, "ML Workflow Execution Mode," mixes training/inference separation, offline versus online execution, and execution instrumentation; split these questions and relocate 34.1–34.3 accordingly. (2) Dimension 30, "Model Packaging and Runtime Placement," combines packaging formats, deployment placement, application architecture, repository selection, and troubleshooting; separate those decision points and move the corresponding values. (3) Dimension 31, "Prediction Serving Mode and Performance," mixes online/batch timing, result delivery, persistence, fallback, freshness, and thresholding; reorganize these into their distinct existing decision topics. (4) Dimension 37, "ML Technology Selection Governance," combines governance, non-functional evaluation, and low-code/boxed toolkit selection; split governance from toolkit/product selection and move values such as 37.4, 37.6, and 37.7. (5) Dimension 46, "ML Code and Asset Organization," combines code structure, asset reuse, documentation, productionization, and generated-code consequences; split the underlying questions and relocate values such as 46.1–46.7 and 46.8–46.13. These structural granularity problems are widespread even though many other dimensions do represent a single decision.

criteria.name: One decision point
criteria.description: Each dimension is a single decision point: all its candidate decisions are alternative answers to one question, rather than a broad topic bundling several questions. Where the use case names quality attributes or forces, dimensions whose choice is driven by recognizable quality attributes or trade-offs are preferred (quality-attribute grounding).
criteria.reason: Many dimensions have at least two candidate decisions and correctly separate outcomes, with strong examples such as 23 Data Labeling Strategy, 19 ML Release Automation, and 31 Prediction Serving Mode and Performance. However, several broad dimensions combine decisions answering different questions. In 34 ML Workflow Execution Mode, training/inference separation, offline training, and execution instrumentation are distinct; merge the first two into 32 ML Workflow Execution Coordination and move 34.3 to 47 ML Dependency and Service Structure. In 46 ML Code and Asset Organization, code style, collaboration, documentation, technology heterogeneity, and generated code are mixed; move 46.3 to 40 ML Organizational and Process Approach and relocate the documentation and technology-structure values to the existing governance or dependency dimensions whose questions they answer. In 40 ML Organizational and Process Approach, team structure, process model, roles, and culture are mixed; split only the team-structure values 40.2 and 40.7 from the process values 40.1, 40.4, and 40.6, while moving the remaining odd values to matching existing decision points. In 3 Training Execution and Scaling Strategy, 3.3 Distributed event computation is not a training decision and should move to 21 Data Ingestion Mechanism. In 48 Neural Architecture Search Strategy, 48.6 Multivariable fraud prediction model is unrelated to neural architecture search and should move to 27 Model Family and Combination Strategy, while 48.7 search-space definition and 48.8 evaluation-metric selection should move to the existing model-selection and evaluation dimensions. These coherence problems are substantial despite the taxonomy's many well-formed, quality-attribute-related decisions.

criteria.name: Rejected-alternative handling
criteria.description: For each candidate decision, the taxonomy makes clear whether sources adopted it, rejected it, or disagree (status 'accepted', 'rejected' or 'mixed'); a rejected alternative is never presented as adopted; each candidate decision appears once with its stance; outcomes (status 'outcome') are kept apart from candidate decisions.
criteria.reason: The taxonomy uses valid status values and many outcomes are correctly expressed as effects, but status-description agreement is violated repeatedly. Mixed values in dimension 44 (ML Interactive Development Environment) and dimension 45 (Notebook Execution Arrangement) are described as adopted practices (“uses” and “are executed”) rather than alternatives on which sources disagree; revise those descriptions to reflect disagreement or change their statuses. The same issue occurs for mixed values such as 39.1–39.2 (MLops Platform Ownership and Sourcing), 41.5 (ML Data Transformation and Feature Engineering), 24.4 (Dataset Access and Availability), 26.4 (Runtime Resource and Performance Strategy), 28.7 (Model Learning, Tuning, and Update Strategy), 29.6 (Model Serving Interface), 30.8, 30.14, 30.15, and 38.2–38.3. Dimension 46 (ML Code and Asset Organization) also presents rejected values 46.5–46.7 as practices that are used, so mark them as declined or change their statuses; conversely, 13.3 (Previously-built-model diff testing) is marked mixed while its description explicitly says it is rejected, so align the status and description. No major violation is evident for the generally effect-oriented outcome values, and no clear duplicate candidate with conflicting statuses is apparent.

criteria.name: Dimensional coverage
criteria.description: Every sampled passage that discusses a design decision can be placed under at least one decision point (dimension) of the taxonomy.
criteria.reason: All decision-bearing passages can be placed under at least one taxonomy dimension. Examples include s19_p09 under automated model-family selection, orchestrated workflows, model serialization, and monitoring; s15_p03 and s02_p03 under data ingestion, preservation, availability, and pipeline execution; s06_p14 and s22_p12 under release, integration, data/model validation, and automated testing; s12_p07 and s16_p07 under serving, repository, and monolith/microservice architecture; and s17_p03 and s18_p04 under hyperparameter optimization and AutoML/toolkit selection. No decision-bearing passage is left without coverage, so there are no corrective issues to report.

criteria.name: Candidate-decision coverage
criteria.description: The options that the sampled passages adopt or reject are named as values (candidate decisions) of the right dimension.
criteria.reason: The taxonomy covers many explicit choices, including AutoML and neural architecture selection in s19_p09, ingestion modes and CDC in s15_p03, CI/CD testing and staged deployment in s06_p14, offline/online serving in s12_p07, and monitoring, drift, and retraining in s23_p10 and s20_p03. Missing options remain: add API-based ingestion to dimension 21 (s15_p03); add language-agnostic and vendor-specific model exchange formats to dimension 30, since s19_p09 explicitly distinguishes both; add manual test execution and the repeated automated-test scoring approach to dimension 14 (s22_p12); add manual production deployment as a distinct value in dimension 19 (s06_p14); and add NoSQL document storage plus scheduled ingestion alternatives to dimensions 43 and 21, respectively (s02_p03). Authentication/access control and product-level safeguards such as email confirmation and 2FA are also adopted options in s14_p01 and s10_p02 but have no corresponding dimension.

criteria.name: Value exclusivity
criteria.description: Each system (source) adopts one value per dimension: the values of a dimension are alternatives, not features used together. Deterministic: computed from the evidence, without a judge.
criteria.reason:
- Dimension 6 'Production Monitoring and Adaptation': 16 of 16 sources adopt several of its values. Values 6.1 'Real-time prediction-quality monitoring' and 6.16 'Production logging and security observability' are adopted together by s01, s04, s08, s18 (passages s01_p06, s04_p02, s04_p03).
- Dimension 31 'Prediction Serving Mode and Performance': 12 of 15 sources adopt several of its values. Values 31.3 'Scheduled batch prediction deployment' and 31.5 'Online computation serving' are adopted together by s02, s12, s15, s19 (passages s02_p02, s02_p12, s02_p13).
- Dimension 23 'Data Labeling Strategy': 4 of 5 sources adopt several of its values. Values 23.1 'Human-in-the-loop data labeling' and 23.2 'Active-learning sample selection' are adopted together by s09, s10, s22, s24 (passages s09_p03, s09_p04, s09_p09).
- Dimension 41 'ML Data Transformation and Feature Engineering': 10 of 13 sources adopt several of its values. Values 41.2 'Automated data preprocessing' and 41.3 'Automated feature engineering' are adopted together by s02, s09, s17, s18 (passages s02_p04, s02_p05, s02_p08).
Values one source uses together are not alternatives. Split such a dimension into the questions its values answer (every part keeps at least two candidate decisions), move a value to the existing dimension whose question it answers, or merge two values that are the same option.

clusters.name: Data Ingestion Mechanism
clusters.description: How source events and records are delivered into ML data workflows.

relations.reading: Choices on Data Ingestion Mechanism affect the outcomes of Training Execution and Scaling Strategy
relations.rationale: Ingestion mode, feature transformations, and available datasets determine training inputs, freshness, and execution requirements.

relations.reading: Choices on Data Ingestion Mechanism affect the outcomes of Production Monitoring and Adaptation
relations.rationale: Feature-generation frequency and incoming-data changes affect model behavior and retraining needs.

values.label: ETL-based feature ingestion
values.description: Batch extraction, transformation, and loading of row-level features from external data sources.

values.label: Streaming feature ingestion
values.description: Continuous or event-driven ingestion of base features from external sources.

values.label: Dual-path event and data ingestion
values.description: Routing interaction inputs simultaneously through low-latency event processing and durable dense-data processing.

values.label: Messaging-based data ingestion
values.description: Ingesting source data through message queues, middleware, or publish-subscribe channels.

values.label: Change-data-capture ingestion
values.description: Ingesting source-system changes through change-data-capture mechanisms.

values.label: Push-based data delivery
values.description: Having source systems push data into databases or pipelines.

values.label: Event-stream data sourcing
values.description: Uses operational event streams as the source for ML data rather than raw database or lake dumps.

values.label: Raw-dump data sourcing
values.description: Sources ML data directly from database dumps or data-lake schemas.

values.label: Query-based data extraction
values.description: Pulling source data by querying and extracting it from other systems.

values.label: Event-stream historical-retention limitation
values.description: Limits training-data history when source events are retained only for a short period.

values.label: Raw-schema coupling and pipeline fragility
values.description: Makes ML data pipelines dependent on changing upstream schemas and inconsistent raw data.

clusters.name: ML Data Transformation and Feature Engineering
clusters.description: How data is preprocessed, transformed, engineered into features, reused, and retired for ML workflows.

values.label: Denormalized or aggregated training dataset
values.description: A cleaned, denormalized, or aggregated feature dataset is materialized as training input.

values.label: Automated data preprocessing
values.description: Automates cleaning, imbalance handling, missing-value treatment, leakage control, and resource-aware preprocessing.

values.label: Automated feature engineering
values.description: Automatically generates and selects features within the ML data pipeline.

values.label: Feature lifecycle cleanup

values.label: Shared data-processing pipeline reuse
values.description: Reuses common ETL, data-quality, and feature-engineering pipelines across teams instead of duplicating them.

values.label: Duplicated data-processing pipelines

clusters.name: ML Data Governance and Preservation

includes.label: Provenance-preserving data ingestion
includes.description: Tracks source origin, metadata, original copies, formats, and privacy handling during ingestion.

includes.label: Immutable original-data preservation

values.label: Cataloged data

includes.label: Dataset metadata cataloging
includes.description: Records dataset size, format, aliases, modification time, access controls, profiling, and versions.

values.label: Privacy- and policy-validated data

includes.label: Programmatic data-policy compliance testing

includes.label: Access-controlled data use

values.label: Integrated end-to-end data governance

includes.label: Analytical datastore selection
includes.description: Selects the warehouse, lake, OLAP system, or analytics database used to expose analytical data.

values.label: Online feature-serving pipeline

includes.label: Data-platform ML pipeline

includes.label: Real-time feature store
includes.description: Streaming and enriched features are materialized in a low-latency store for model use.

values.label: Durable end-to-end feature platform
values.description: An end-to-end platform prepares data, serves features in real time, and persists engineered feature data for reuse in training, recovery, and subsequent inference.

includes.label: Durable feature data store

values.label: Online/offline feature-store architecture
values.description: Features are maintained in complementary online and durable stores, separating low-latency inference access from persistent training and reuse needs.

includes.label: Durable feature data store
includes.description: Persists engineered features for long-term reuse, training, and recovery.

values.label: Distributed feature-retrieval architecture outcome

clusters.name: Data Labeling Strategy

values.label: Human-in-the-loop data labeling
values.description: Uses domain experts and controlled review workflows to create labels for ML datasets.

values.label: Active-learning sample selection
values.description: Programmatically selects uncertain or error-prone production inputs for labeling.

clusters.name: Dataset Access and Availability
clusters.description: How datasets are exposed, extracted, sourced, materialized, and kept available to ML workflows.

values.label: API-mediated dataset access
values.description: Training and evaluation services obtain their respective datasets through a dedicated segregation or access API.

values.label: Local consolidation of external data
values.description: Persisting externally served data with local records to avoid repeated runtime service queries.

values.label: External curated dataset sourcing
values.description: Using a named external repository or curated dataset as the training-data source.

values.label: Local sensitive-data storage
values.description: Keeping sensitive ML data on local machines rather than in protected server-side storage.

values.label: Data availability and throughput requirements
values.description: Setting source-data availability, processing-speed, and scalability requirements for ingestion and access.

values.label: Online data-source availability requirement
values.description: Serving requires relevant feature and context data sources to remain available online.

clusters.name: Training Execution and Scaling Strategy
clusters.description: Varies how training workloads execute, scale, and allocate compute, independently of which predictive algorithm is selected.

relations.reading: Choices on Training Execution and Scaling Strategy affect the outcomes of Model Family and Combination Strategy
relations.rationale: Incremental, parallel, or distributed execution changes which algorithms, update methods, and model candidates are practical.

relations.reading: Choices on Training Execution and Scaling Strategy limit the options available on Runtime State and Communication Strategy
relations.rationale: Training scale and memory behavior determine suitable hardware, state handling, and resource allocation.

values.label: Vertically scalable training
values.description: Training scales primarily by using a larger machine rather than distributing computation across machines.

values.label: Horizontal and vertical training scalability
values.description: Scales training by adding resources or increasing capacity of existing resources.

values.label: Distributed event computation
values.description: Executing high-volume event processing across distributed computation infrastructure.

values.label: Fault-tolerant partitioned training
values.description: Uses checkpoints, error tolerance, and failover to recover partitioned training after transient failures.

values.label: Parallel candidate training
values.description: Multiple algorithms, parameter combinations, or candidate models are trained concurrently for comparison.

values.label: Distributed-training scalability requirement
values.description: An outcome indicating that training requires distributed execution or scaling beyond a single computation context.

clusters.name: Model Family and Combination Strategy
clusters.description: Which predictive model families or combinations are selected for the ML solution.

relations.reading: Choices on Model Family and Combination Strategy affect the outcomes of Model Evaluation and Regression Strategy
relations.rationale: Different learner families require different evaluation criteria, tests, and acceptable performance trade-offs.

relations.reading: Choices on Model Family and Combination Strategy affect the outcomes of Runtime State and Communication Strategy
relations.rationale: Model complexity and prediction representation influence serving memory, latency, and hardware requirements.

values.label: Automated model-family selection
values.description: The solution automatically selects among learner families according to predictive performance, computational cost, or workflow objectives, without requiring a dedicated model-building service or ensemble.

includes.label: Automated model-family selection
includes.description: Selects among alternative learner families according to predictive score, time, or workflow objectives.

values.label: Service-based configurable model building
values.description: A reusable model-building service trains and selects models through configurable algorithms, parameters, and metrics. It can support interchangeable learner implementations and specified families such as random forests.

includes.label: Random forest learner
includes.description: Random forests are selected when their precision-recall balance fits the intended application.

includes.label: Automated model-family selection
includes.description: Selects among alternative learner families according to predictive score, time, or workflow objectives.

includes.label: Dedicated model-builder service
includes.description: Separates candidate training and metric-driven model selection into a reusable model-building service.

includes.label: Interchangeable model-algorithm library
includes.description: Uses a replaceable library of algorithms so model types can be added and exchanged in training pipelines.

values.label: Ensemble-oriented automated modeling
values.description: The solution combines multiple models, potentially using an automated or packaged AutoML process to select and blend them for improved predictive performance or stability.

includes.label: Automated model-family selection
includes.description: Selects among alternative learner families according to predictive score, time, or workflow objectives.

includes.label: Model ensembling
includes.description: Combines multiple trained models to improve stability or predictive score.

includes.label: Boxed AutoML tool
includes.description: Packaged off-the-shelf AutoML is rejected as the chosen modeling approach.

values.label: Fixed learner-and-objective configuration
values.description: The solution uses a deliberately specified predictive learner together with a task-specific objective, such as gradient-boosted trees with a binary logistic objective.

includes.label: Gradient-boosted tree learner
includes.description: Using gradient-boosted decision trees as the predictive model family.

includes.label: Binary logistic objective
includes.description: Configuring a learner with a Bernoulli/logistic objective for binary classification.

values.label: Nonlinear online learner
values.description: A nonlinear learner is considered for online data but rejected when its adaptation speed is insufficient.

clusters.name: Model Learning, Tuning, and Update Strategy
clusters.description: How selected models learn, tune, update, and adapt during training and operation.

values.label: Linear online learner
values.description: Linear or logistic regression is used for efficient, explainable, parameter-only online prediction.

values.label: Feature-enhanced linear learner
values.description: Feature engineering, interaction terms, or hashing extend a linear learner's representation capacity.

values.label: Incremental online training
values.description: Models are updated incrementally as new data arrives, using optimization suited to online learning.

values.label: Automated hyperparameter optimization
values.description: Searches model configuration and training hyperparameters automatically.

values.label: Manual hyperparameter tuning
values.description: Uses hand-selected trial-and-error experiments to tune model hyperparameters.

values.label: Model optimization objective selection
values.description: Selects the performance objective or error type that automated model optimization should prioritize.

values.label: Client-side model training
values.description: Trains models on client devices rather than in a centralized server environment.

values.label: Federated model-update learning
values.description: Models learn through exchanging model updates rather than transferring personal training data to a central server.

values.label: Near-real-time model adaptation
values.description: Updating models rapidly as incoming examples change the observed data distribution.

values.label: Near-real-time learning and inference
values.description: Supporting model learning and inference with near-real-time responsiveness.

values.label: Hyperparameter search-space burden
values.description: Large or exponentially growing hyperparameter spaces make manual optimization costly and slow.

clusters.name: Model Evaluation and Regression Strategy
clusters.description: Varies how model quality and regressions are assessed before promotion.

relations.reading: Choices on Model Evaluation and Regression Strategy affect the outcomes of Production Monitoring and Adaptation
relations.rationale: Pre-production thresholds and validation criteria establish the quality signals later monitored for regression and decay.

relations.reading: Model Evaluation and Regression Strategy requires ML Workflow Execution Coordination to be decided first
relations.rationale: Automated integration, regression, and canary checks depend on the workflow and release path being established.

values.label: Offline evaluation pipeline
values.description: Candidate models are evaluated against held-out data and true values before deployment selection.

values.label: Threshold-based quality regression testing
values.description: Quality thresholds detect gradual degradation across versions and sudden drops in a new model.

values.label: Previously-built-model diff testing
values.description: Direct diff-testing against previously built ML models is explicitly rejected because it is difficult to maintain.

values.label: Held-out test-set isolation
values.description: Keeps a sampled test set unseen during model selection to prevent data snooping.

values.label: Interpretability-oriented model evaluation
values.description: Evaluates or explains model behavior to support compliance and understanding of predictions.

values.label: Metric-driven candidate model evaluation
values.description: Evaluates multiple candidate models on validation data using a selected performance metric.

values.label: Risk-specific model evaluation
values.description: Evaluating models against the particular harms or attack categories relevant to the business.

values.label: Business-impact-aligned evaluation
values.description: Evaluating models by whether algorithmic metrics correlate with business outcomes and user impact.

values.label: Fairness and inclusion evaluation
values.description: Testing model performance for fairness, bias, inclusion, and protected-category effects.

values.label: Model staleness testing
values.description: Testing whether outdated data or business-impact performance makes a model stale.

values.label: Separated training and test-data collection
values.description: Keeping procedures and teams for training and test data collection methodologically independent.

values.label: Feature predictive-power evaluation
values.description: Tests whether candidate features improve predictive performance before inclusion.

values.label: Feature infrastructure cost evaluation
values.description: Compares feature latency, dependencies, and memory costs against predictive value.

values.label: Single-objective evaluation
values.description: Treats one aggregate error-minimization objective as the sole basis for model evaluation.

values.label: Ground-truth quality assessment
values.description: Assessing label accuracy as a determinant and upper bound of model quality.

clusters.name: ML Integration Testing Strategy
clusters.description: Varies how pipeline integration and production readiness are validated across components and environments.

values.label: Automated full-pipeline integration testing
values.description: The complete data, code, training, and evaluation pipeline is repeatedly executed and validated.

values.label: Production canary validation
values.description: A model is loaded into production and checked on real-life data before wider serving.

values.label: Prediction API contract testing
values.description: Checks expected request and response contracts after model or service changes.

values.label: Prediction-service load and latency testing
values.description: Tests serving throughput and response latency under operational load.

values.label: Training health validation
values.description: Validates convergence and numerical health, including absence of NaN results.

values.label: Target-infrastructure compatibility testing
values.description: Checks package, memory, compute, and accelerator compatibility with the serving environment.

values.label: Feature and model unit testing
values.description: Tests feature-engineering logic and model methods for implementation defects.

values.label: Schema and domain validation testing
values.description: Validates data and feature schemas and domains across training and serving stages.

values.label: Automated data-and-model validation
values.description: Automatically validates training data and models before retraining or deployment.

clusters.name: Production Monitoring and Adaptation
clusters.description: Varies how deployed systems observe quality, data changes, resource behavior, and trigger corrective model-development actions.

relations.reading: Choices on Production Monitoring and Adaptation affect the outcomes of Model Family and Combination Strategy
relations.rationale: Observed decay, bias, or changing input distributions can prompt a different learner or a new model version.

values.label: Real-time prediction-quality monitoring
values.description: Prediction quality and model behavior are measured immediately or continuously after serving when labels are available.

values.label: Input and feature-drift monitoring
values.description: Feature-generation processes, schemas, statistical values, and unusual inputs are monitored for changes.

values.label: Threshold-based retraining
values.description: Quality degradation or data-value shifts trigger retraining, while schema anomalies halt execution for investigation.

values.label: Passive production operation
values.description: The system does not actively track predictions or model performance after deployment.

values.label: Automated retraining pipeline
values.description: Automatically retrains models using new production or labeled data.

values.label: Schedule-based retraining trigger
values.description: Starts retraining on recurring daily, weekly, or monthly schedules.

values.label: Data-availability retraining trigger
values.description: Starts retraining when newly collected training data becomes available.

values.label: Performance- or drift-based retraining trigger
values.description: Starts retraining after model degradation or feature-distribution drift is detected.

values.label: Business-impact monitoring
values.description: Monitors decision quality, business goals, risks, fairness, segments, and use-case-specific error costs.

values.label: Software-metrics-only monitoring
values.description: Limits monitoring to generic software metrics without ML quality or impact measures.

values.label: Downstream-KPI-only monitoring
values.description: Relies exclusively on delayed downstream business KPIs to detect model problems.

values.label: Automated failure recovery

values.label: Production logging and security observability

values.label: Model-decay planning

values.label: Periodic model health checks

values.label: User-reported model issue detection

values.label: Custom model-monitoring dashboard

values.label: Ad hoc model-insight analysis

values.label: Separate model and business-KPI monitoring

values.label: Service-health and data-quality monitoring

values.label: Root-cause performance diagnosis

values.label: Compute-optimized training hardware

values.label: Scale-to-zero serving
values.description: Reduces serving capacity to zero when demand falls to control operating cost.

values.label: CPU-or-GPU resource allocation
values.description: Selects CPU or GPU capacity as a service for cluster job execution.

values.label: Replicated mutable model instances
values.description: Replicating model instances behind load balancing for serving or learning workloads.

values.label: Full-dataset in-memory retention
values.description: Keeping the complete training dataset in memory during model updates.

values.label: Elastic resource scaling

values.label: Large-scale data processing capacity

values.label: Service resource and latency profiling

values.label: CPU and memory sizing guidance

values.label: ONNX performance improvement

values.label: Extended fraud-decision latency

clusters.name: Model Serving Interface
clusters.description: How deployed models expose prediction interfaces and exchange model inputs and outputs.

values.label: REST prediction microservice
values.description: A model is exposed through an API-backed prediction microservice for application integration.

values.label: PMML-based model serving
values.description: PMML provides a portable model representation that supports compatible tooling and both online and distributed batch scoring.

values.label: Multi-source model input interface
values.description: An algorithm or serving interface that accepts trained models, processed data, and fresh live signals as distinct inputs.

values.label: Parallelized service data access
values.description: Obtaining independent service data concurrently rather than serially when assembling model-serving inputs.

values.label: Cross-service identifier translation
values.description: Mapping application identifiers to external service identifiers before retrieving model-serving data.

values.label: Adoption of external service identifiers
values.description: Using a third-party service's identifier as the application's primary lookup key.

values.label: gRPC model interface
values.description: Exposing an independently deployed model through a gRPC interface.

values.label: Socket-based model interface
values.description: Using socket communication as the client-server interface for model-serving requests.

clusters.name: Model Packaging and Runtime Placement
clusters.description: How models are packaged and placed into application, container, edge, or service runtimes.

values.label: Containerized offline prediction service
values.description: A containerized service loads a model for on-demand or scheduled batch prediction.

values.label: Monolithic application architecture
values.description: The model is integrated within a single monolithic application structure.

values.label: Model-as-a-service deployment
values.description: Exposes predictions as a real-time model service integrated with product applications.

values.label: On-device edge inference
values.description: Runs model inference in deployed edge modules on hardware devices.

values.label: Amalgamated standalone model package
values.description: Packages model logic and runtime code into one portable deployable artifact.

values.label: Cross-format model serialization
values.description: Uses interoperable representations such as PFA, ONNX, or generated code for model serving.

values.label: Repository selection by workload
values.description: Selecting among storage repositories according to access patterns, consistency, latency, and workload needs.

values.label: Microservice integration architecture
values.description: Integrating ML capabilities through independently organized services rather than one application unit.

values.label: Hybrid microservice-monolith architecture
values.description: Combining independently separated services with shared components in one application architecture.

values.label: Long-running serving daemon
values.description: Keeping the model-serving server alive for the application's lifetime with maintenance interruptions.

values.label: Plug-in model architecture
values.description: Deployment architecture allows new recommendation or model approaches to be integrated as replaceable components.

values.label: Automatic container image generation
values.description: Creates the deployment container image automatically as part of model deployment.

values.label: Manually specified deployment image
values.description: Requires practitioners to specify the production container image used for deployment.

values.label: Strict microservice deployment architecture
values.description: Uses a strict microservice-oriented architecture for ML project deployment.

values.label: Client-side prediction placement
values.description: Places prediction execution on client devices rather than on a server.

values.label: Local deployment troubleshooting
values.description: Deploys a model locally to diagnose and debug production deployment problems.

values.label: Client-server prediction architecture
values.description: Places prediction requests and execution across client and server components.

values.label: Model-as-dependency deployment
values.description: The model is packaged and deployed with the consuming application for build-time and runtime availability.

values.label: Containerized inference deployment
values.description: Packages inference code and dependencies in a container for deployment across managed, on-premise, or hybrid runtimes.

values.label: Serverless zip-package deployment
values.description: Places serverless application code and dependencies in a zip artifact with a single entry point.

values.label: Direct deployment of offline-trained model
values.description: Deploys an offline-trained model directly as a prediction service without the required production conversion workflow.

values.label: Traditional Hadoop production architecture
values.description: Using a Hadoop-based architecture for production ML and fraud-processing workloads.

values.label: Container-orchestrated ML runtime
values.description: Runs containerized ML workloads under an orchestrator such as Kubernetes or a managed serverless container service.

values.label: Layered ML pipeline architecture
values.description: Separates data, computation, and serving-orchestration layers in the ML execution workflow.

values.label: Independent component deployment outcome
values.description: An outcome in which ML components are deployed independently rather than as one combined unit.

values.label: Interleaved model dependency outcome
values.description: An outcome in which model dependencies become interleaved across application components.

values.label: Weak ML component boundaries outcome
values.description: An outcome in which ML components have weak architectural boundaries.

values.label: Serverless artifact-size constraint
values.description: Limits feasible serverless model deployment because packaged code and dependencies must fit platform artifact-size limits.

clusters.name: Prediction Serving Mode and Performance
clusters.description: When and how predictions are computed, delivered, persisted, recovered, and kept fresh in production.

values.label: Queue-fronted online serving cluster
values.description: Containerized online predictors are distributed across servers behind a queue for load balancing, throughput, and low latency.

values.label: Serverless function deployment
values.description: ML workloads are packaged as functions and executed through a serverless runtime with automated scaling and operational handling.

values.label: Scheduled batch prediction deployment
values.description: Deploys scheduled batch scoring and writes results to storage or analytics systems.

values.label: Report-based result delivery
values.description: Delivers predictions through dashboards, webhooks, SMS, or email reports.

values.label: Online computation serving
values.description: Computing predictions from current context and recent data during an online request.

values.label: Precomputed offline serving
values.description: Producing predictions in advance through periodic or batch computation for later serving.

values.label: Precomputed-result fallback
values.description: Serving an existing precomputed result when online computation cannot satisfy availability or latency requirements.

values.label: Offline-online serving parity
values.description: Keeping model behavior consistent between offline and online prediction contexts.

values.label: Hybrid offline-online serving
values.description: Combining precomputed results with online processing to add freshness at request time.

values.label: Production prediction persistence
values.description: Persisting production inputs and predictions for later monitoring, analysis, or evaluation.

values.label: Candidate-user assignment
values.description: Selecting users for shadow, canary, or A/B model exposure using lists, attributes, geography, or randomization.

values.label: Prediction-serving fallback behavior
values.description: Returning fallback results when online feature retrieval or inputs are unavailable or anomalous.

values.label: Threshold-based prediction decision
values.description: A prediction score is converted into an operational action through a configured threshold.

values.label: Probability-valued prediction output
values.description: Returning a probability or likelihood score rather than only a categorical prediction.

values.label: Recommendation-result staleness
values.description: Prediction results become stale because offline computation does not reflect recent context or data.

values.label: Nearline computation serving
values.description: Serving computations in an intermediate mode that is fresher than offline processing without strict real-time response.

values.label: Real-time recommendation infeasibility
values.description: Inability to meet real-time recommendation serving requirements because computation and feature calls are too slow.

values.label: Gradient-based architecture search
values.description: Uses a continuous relaxation and gradients to search neural-network architectures.
